problem: Goal-driven street-view navigation RL agents (StreetLearn courier task) cannot transfer to unseen city areas without extensive retraining, and collecting new street-level imagery or building simulators is expensive.
motivation: Aerial imagery is cheap and globally available, and humans adapt to a new city by studying a map before navigating at street level. The paper uses aerial views as an auxiliary modality to adapt a ground-view agent to a new region without any ground-view data in that region.
key_idea: Pair ground and aerial views and learn a view-invariant policy (L2 embedding loss, KL policy distillation between the two pathways, and view dropout), so the agent can be adapted to a new area with aerial views only and then deployed on ground views.
insight: The embedding-only loss is insufficient: the ablation (Fig. 7) shows the full model beats 'embed+dropout' (no KL) clearly. Replacing view dropout with one-way 'view distillation' (always acting on the ground logits) is decent but non-trivially worse, so dropout forces the policy to be interchangeable across views. The adaptation stage matters most for zero-shot reward and early learning, especially without heading information. Its effect fades once agents are fully retrained (Fig. 6).
method: Two-stream agent: separate CNNs for ground and aerial 84x84 images, with a locale LSTM (region-specific) and a policy LSTM (shared across regions) both shared across the two views; architecture extends Mirowski et al. 2018 (courier task).
Joint embedding loss: L2 distance between the ground CNN embedding and the aerial CNN embedding at the same location (lambda=1).
Policy distillation: KL divergence between the softmax policy logits of the ground and aerial pathways (gamma=1).
View dropout: a gating layer randomly selects the ground or aerial policy logits for action sampling at each step, forcing interchangeable policies.

Three-stage transfer: (1) train on 4 regions with both views, all modules trained, 1B steps; (2) adapt to the target region with aerial-only observations, training only the target locale LSTM, 500M steps; (3) transfer to ground-view only in the target region, with CNNs and policy LSTM frozen and only the target locale LSTM trained.

Training: IMPALA with 256 actors (single-region) or 512 (multi-region), curriculum and reward shaping, optional auxiliary heading prediction. StreetAir testbed adds aerial images to StreetLearn for NYC and Pittsburgh.

setting.backbone: CNN + locale LSTM + policy LSTM two-stream actor-critic (IMPALA), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: RL in StreetLearn/StreetAir: 4 training regions (Downtown NYC, Midtown NYC, Allegheny Pittsburgh, CMU area), 1B steps, then 500M steps of aerial-only adaptation in the held-out region (NYU/Union Square NYC)
setting.observation: 84x84 ground-view Street View panorama crop; aerial 84x84 image (train/adapt only), rotated to the agent heading; goal as lat/long
setting.action_space: 5 discrete actions: move forward, turn left/right 22.5°, turn left/right 67.5°
setting.simulator: StreetLearn / StreetAir (Google Street View + aerial images)
setting.privileged: Aerial images of the target region during adaptation only (not at test time); optional heading supervision and curriculum in some experiments

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out NYU/Union Square NYC region, zero-shot reward averaged over 350M steps
numbers.method: Cross-view (full model, adaptation on aerial only)
numbers.extra: 3-stage transfer with aerial-only adaptation; curriculum; no heading; locale LSTM retrained during transfer
numbers.evidence: The proposed cross-view method achieves a zero-shot reward of 29 ... 34.5% zero-shot success rate ... (580 vs. 500)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmarks; results are on the paper's own StreetAir environment, and most results appear in figures only. The single-view baseline had zero-shot reward 5, SR 10.5%, 50@100M, 200@200M and convergence reward 500.
results: Cross-view transfer reaches a zero-shot reward of 29 and 34.5% success, versus 5 and 10.5% for the single-view baseline. It also learns faster (190 vs 50 at 100M steps) and converges higher (580 vs 500). Ablations show that the KL loss, view dropout and the aerial adaptation stage each contribute.
limitations: Evaluated only on one held-out NYC region in a single environment, with a custom StreetAir benchmark and mostly figure-based results.
Requires paired aerial and ground imagery in the source regions, and aerial images of the target area, with a heading-aligned rotation; the courier task also requires a curriculum.
Advantage of adaptation shrinks after full retraining; a gap remains without curriculum/heading in single-view baselines.
builds_on: StreetLearn courier task agent (Mirowski et al. 2018)
compares_to: Single-view (ground-only) multi-city agent of Mirowski et al. 2018
Cross-view with view distillation instead of dropout
